classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a parallelogram's area, use the stated area relationship, then solve for the rectangle's height while retaining a redundant sloping-side measurement.

inlines.text: The area of the parallelogram is twice the area of the rectangle.
Work out the height of the rectangle.

spec.description: Unfilled parallelogram leaning right, with matching single parallel arrows on horizontal sides and matching double parallel arrows on sloping sides. External dimension arrows label the base and left sloping side; an internal vertical dimension arrow labels the perpendicular height.
spec.mathematics: Base 12 cm, perpendicular height 7 cm and sloping side 9 cm. The redundant 9 cm measurement is retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements are visible; no calculated area or rectangle height is shown.

spec.description: Unfilled upright rectangle with an external horizontal width arrow below and an external vertical height arrow to the left.
spec.mathematics: Width 8 cm and unknown height x cm. Drawing coordinates reproduce the source appearance and do not specify another measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown height remains labelled x cm; its calculated value is absent.

answer.worked:
Let $A_p$ be the parallelogram's area and $A_r$ the rectangle's area.
$$\begin{align*}
A_p &= bh\\
A_p &= 12\times7\\
A_p &= 84\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
The rectangle has half this area.
$$\begin{align*}
A_r &= 84\div2\\
A_r &= 42\text{ cm}^2\\
A_r &= lw\\
42 &= 8x\\
\frac{42}{8} &= x\\
5.25\text{ cm} &= x
\end{align*}$$
